paragraphs: Friend, this passage is a whole lot of names, and I get it. But here's what I love: the LORD has His people counted, tribe by tribe and clan by clan. Every family line is written down, and the land would be given out "according to the names of the tribes of their fathers" (Numbers 26:55).

Now look at what He does with that count. He promised a land, and He's about to hand it over, share by share, by lot (Numbers 26:53-56). Even the Levites, who are not numbered with the other Israelites, get their own list, because "no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites" (Numbers 26:62). Counted doesn't mean the same share. It means nobody got lost in the shuffle.

And then the sting at the end. Of everyone counted at Sinai, "Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun" (Numbers 26:65). The LORD had said they would die in the wilderness, and what He says, He does. Which means His promises of inheritance stand just as firm, so keep your ovens ready, friend, and trust the One who keeps His word.
